report.experiment: Rigid pendulum — rod with a wooden block
report.headline: Using the lab length of 33 cm and a measured period of 1.1596 s, the pendulum gives g = 9.80 ± 0.09 m/s², in agreement with the standard 9.80665 m/s².
report.law: θ(t) = θ0·e^(−γt)·cos(2πt/T + φ), with T = 2π√(L/g) including a finite-amplitude correction; here L = 33 cm and amplitude θ0 ≈ 17.5°

results.note: From pendulum fit with L = 33.0 ± 0.3 cm; uncertainty is dominated by the ±0.3 cm (±0.9%) length uncertainty, the period contribution is negligible. 0.04% below standard g.
Measured over the fitted window 1.633–4.900 s; small-angle period from the same fit is 1.15282 s, showing the finite-amplitude correction at 17.5° matters at the ~0.6% level.
Initial angular amplitude from the pendulum fit; moderate amplitude, so the finite-amplitude pendulum model is preferred over a pure cosine.
Corresponds to a quality factor Q ≈ 447, i.e. very light damping over the ~3 observed cycles; damping is therefore poorly constrained compared with the period.

results.quantity: Arc radius of tracked block centroid
results.note: Geometric distance from fitted pivot to the tracked wooden-block centroid. For this rigid pendulum this is not the given 33 cm pivot-to-centre-of-mass/effective length, so it was not used as a pixel-to-cm calibration and any difference is not an error.

comparisons.model: Pendulum fit (fit_model, L = 33 cm, finite amplitude)
comparisons.verdict: Best physical description: angle RMS 0.086° (0.0015 rad), arc RMS 0.41 px, no warnings; gives g = 9.803 ± 0.089 m/s². No BIC is returned by fit_model.

comparisons.model: Damped cosine θ = A·exp(−γt)·cos(ωt + p) on angle
comparisons.verdict: Favoured over the undamped cosine by ΔBIC = 7.6, which is suggestive but not decisive (decisive is >10). RMS is in rad. It is only a small-angle approximation to the pendulum motion.

comparisons.model: Undamped cosine θ = A·cos(ωt + p) on angle
comparisons.verdict: Slightly worse than the damped cosine (ΔBIC = 7.6) and worse than the finite-amplitude pendulum fit; its near-competitiveness is consistent with very light damping over only about three cycles.

data_quality: Tracking is clean: 117 points from 1.033 to 4.900 s with no gaps (largest gap 0 frames); the fit used 99 points from 1.633 to 4.900 s, starting 0.2 s after the 1.433 s release.
Fit residuals are small: arc RMS 0.41 px and angular RMS 0.086°, with no fit warnings.

There is no pixel scale in this run. This does not affect g because the period is scale-free and the lab length L = 33 cm was supplied; however the result relies entirely on that length, whose ±0.3 cm uncertainty dominates the ±0.09 m/s² error on g.
Only about three cycles are observed, so the period is precise but the small damping rate/Q is weakly constrained.
The 522 px arc radius is the pivot-to-tracked-block-centroid distance for a rigid rod-plus-block pendulum, not the given centre-of-mass/effective length, so it was not converted with the 33 cm value.
report.explanation: A wooden block on a rod swings back and forth like a clock pendulum, completing one swing every 1.16 seconds. Because the time for a pendulum swing depends on its length and on gravity, combining that very precise timing with the lab-measured 33 cm length gives the strength of gravity. The result, 9.80 ± 0.09 metres per second squared, matches the accepted Earth value. The swing barely fades during the video, showing friction and air resistance are very small here.
next_steps: Measure the effective pendulum length more precisely than ±0.3 cm, since this dominates the uncertainty in g.
Film many more cycles to pin down the tiny damping and improve the period further.
Add an independent ruler scale in the plane of swing to convert the 522 px arc radius to centimetres as a geometric cross-check (while keeping it distinct from the centre-of-mass length).
Repeat at a smaller release angle to verify the finite-amplitude correction.

meta.notes: Rigid pendulum: a rod with a wooden block on the end. 33 cm from the pivot to the centre of mass (given by the lab)
